paras: The police killing of Daniels took place on August 18, 1910, when Officer Hebert Waites shot dead a Black man named Daniels after a call to Howell Street, apparently in Shreveport, Louisiana. According to the police account, the only one published, Daniels struck at the officer with a hatchet while being taken to the station, and an inquest was set for that evening.
Daniels was described as a man "said to have gone crazy on religion." He had only recently been released from jail, where he had been held "for being crazy."

Police were told that Daniels, armed with a shotgun, was "terrorizing the people on Howell street." Officer Waites went to the scene, calmed Daniels and persuaded him to lay down the gun. As the two walked toward the station, Waites said, Daniels drew a hatchet from his waist and struck at him; the officer warded off the blow and fired the fatal shot.

An inquest was announced for the evening of the shooting. No report of its finding, of any charge against the officer, or of a statement from Daniels's family or other witnesses appears in the coverage.

The Shreveport Caucasian carried the story on its front page on the day of the shooting under the headline "CRAZY NEGRO SHOT" and the deck "He Is Killed by Officer Hebert Waites of the Police." The brief item gave the officer's version of the hatchet attack as fact and offered no other account. No other white paper and no Black paper was found to have reported the killing.

reader.title: Police killing of Daniels in Shreveport
bases: A police officer shot and killed Daniels while taking him to the station; no crowd or mob is mentioned (A1).
Only one report, in a Shreveport paper, was found in either press, and it gives the police account (A1).
